newsitem.title: CANADA: Amber Energy boosts '98 financial estimates.
newsitem.headline: Amber Energy boosts '98 financial estimates.

text.p: Amber Energy Inc, whose big Alberta heavy oil play has been a hot topic at an industry conference this week, increased projected financial results for 1998, Amber chief executive Richard Lewankski said on Tuesday.

Lewanski told analysts and portfolio managers at the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers Investment Symposium that Amber boosted its cash flow estimates for 1998 to C$130 million or C$2.45 a share, based on plans to drill 75 wells at Pelican Lake this winter.

That would bring the total number of wells on the play by March to 111, yielding expected production of 20,000 barrels per day of oil. Average output at Pelican Lake last year was 4,000 barrels a day.
Amber expects its 1997 cash flow to be C$75 million or C$1.45 a share this year, up from C$43.7 million or C$0.95 a share in 1996, Lewanski said.
The company's net earnings were projected at C$20 million or C$0.39 a share for 1997 and C$34 million or C$0.65 a share for 1998. It posted earnings in 1996 of C$11.9 million or C$0.26 a share.

Amber, whose stock price has soared over the past year on the potential of the northeast Alberta heavy oil play, has 100 percent interest in 143 sections of land, making it the largest landholder in the red-hot area.

On Monday, Canadian Natural Resources Ltd, said it paid a rich C$45 million for 58 sections of land at Pelican Lake and Alberta Energy Co Ltd said it paid C$16 million for a land spread about a third the size of CNQ's at a recent land sale.
Analysts peg the play's total oil in place at 3 billion barrels, with as much as 400 million barrels recoverable.
Lewanski said Amber's total production was projected at 19,500 barrels of oil equivalent per day 1997 and 35,000 in 1998. The company pumped out an average 11,277 BOE a day in 1996.
The average well at Pelican Lake produces about 250 barrels of 16 degree API oil a day for Amber without costly enhanced recovery methods, Lewanski told reporters.
He said he estimated total reserves per well at 300,000 barrels.

Amber currently has 100 million barrels of reserves booked at Pelican Lake that are considered recoverable using conventional methods and Lewanski said the company would likely increase that to 150 million barrels with recently acquired land.
Last November, proven plus probable heavy oil reserves at Pelican Lake were booked at 22 million barrels.
Amber stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange was unchanged on Tuesday at 17. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
